messages:
Mia: Quick publish of the perf runs for saffron-6o (int4 path) on A100s — posting the short summary + artifacts. TL;DR: steady-state throughput looks good but tail spikes under burst. See details below.

Mia: Config used: seq=512, batch=1/4/8 sweep, quant=int4, kv-cache=on, prefix-caching=on. Run id: saffron-6o/1728802468. Artifact: https://perf.redwood/internal/saffron/1728802468 

Mia: Key numbers (local lab, single GPU):
```
b=1  => 120 tokens/s  (p50 42ms, p95 190ms, p99 480ms)
b=4  => 420 tokens/s  (p50 38ms, p95 200ms, p99 510ms)
b=8  => 780 tokens/s  (p50 36ms, p95 210ms, p99 560ms)
notes: steady-state throughput stable after warmup, cold-start p99 is ~1.2s for some prompts
```

perf-bot: Automated profile attached: flamegraph + allocator trace (saffron-6o/1728802468).

Kevin: Nice summary. Did you see any KV-cache evictions during the run? p99 looks high for cold starts.

Mia: KV-cache evictions yes but only after sustained >2 minute sessions; observed cache growth to ~1.2GB then stable. Prefix hit-rate on our test corpus ~82%. Cold-start p99 correlates with first-token generation and scheduler ramp.

Priya: Can you drop the raw command and the bench script you used? Need it to reproduce in dedicated CI.

Mia: Sure — command I used: 
```
./bench_runner --model saffron-6o --seq 512 --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --quant int4 --device a100 --kv-cache on --out saffron/1728802468
```
Script is in the artifact bundle.

Sam: How does this compare to alpine-6b (our current default for quick prod)? Any regressions or wins we should flag?

Mia: vs alpine-6b (same hardware): saffron-6o +18% throughput at b=8, p50 latency ~30ms better. However p99 is ~12% worse on saffron under bursty arrival patterns. Likely due to attention kernel interaction + slightly larger KV working set.

Kevin: Got it. Can you try a micro-profiling pass with KV-heavy prompts (long prefix) and a second pass with tiny prefix to isolate kernel stalls? I suspect a particular fused-kernel path is regressing.

Mia: Added to follow-ups. Also flagged a separate kernel-tuning experiment (flip kernel flag X) to see p99 impact.

Dexter: Ops note — for Dedicated/Canary rollout I recommend capping burst concurrency to 2x steady for saffron until we confirm p99 fixes. I created INF-2345 to track the rollout plan + rollback thresholds. @Mia please link artifacts to the ticket.

Priya: I'll need the artifact link in the perf dashboard and a short one-paragraph callout for the model catalog entry (behavioral notes + recommended config).

Mia: Will add catalog blurb and link the dashboard. Plan: run micro-profiling (Kevin) + kernel flag sweep (Mia) + small canary with burst cap (Dexter). Target: re-run full sweep next Tue and update the ticket.

Kevin: On micro-profiling, ETA EOD today. Will post traces.

Sam: If the micro-profiling suggests a kernel path regression, should we consider falling back to alpine-6b for low-latency slices until kernel fix is validated?

Mia: Yep, fallback policy is in INF-2345. We'll coordinate with product for any critical path changes.

Dexter: Noted. I also scheduled a 30m sync tomorrow 10:30 to walk through traces if folks want to join.

Mia: Thanks all — marking this thread as published summary. Follow-ups: add artifact to ticket INF-2345, run Kevin's micro-profiling, test kernel-flag sweep b=6 as an intermediate point, prepare short catalog note. :tada:
